note: CD20 depleters in FL: epcoritamab (CD3xCD20) approved 2024 on humanized-mouse, monkey and ex-vivo data; veltuzumab active in phase I/II then dropped; MIL62 phase 1b/2 positive but no public model data read; imvotamab without published FL results.
label: Follicular lymphoma (CD20 depleters)

engagement.note: Veltuzumab at low doses depleted circulating and sessile B cells in normal cynomolgus monkeys; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.quote: Studies of intraperitoneal and subcutaneous doses in mouse models of human lymphoma and in normal cynomolgus monkeys disclosed that low doses of veltuzumab control tumor growth or deplete circulating or sessile B cells.

engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral B-cell depletion after first dose, monkey vs patient
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed). Registry record for the veltuzumab phase I/II (IMMU-106-01) not located.
engagement.note: Veltuzumab depleted peripheral B cells after the first infusion at every dose (80-750 mg/m2) in relapsed NHL, 55 of 82 patients FL.
engagement.short: B cells depleted at all doses
engagement.quote: At all dose levels studied, B cells were depleted after the first infusion, veltuzumab serum half-lives were similar after the fourth infusion
engagement.reason: B cells depleted as monkeys showed
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Goldenberg 2009 (monkey) with Morschhauser 2009 (patients). Peripheral B-cell depletion read as the target cell's own removal (proximal). Epcoritamab later repeated the match (Engelberts 2020 monkey; Hutchings 2021 'robust and sustained B-cell depletion'), which changes no status, so it is not a separate entry.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); FDA BLA 761324 review confirms the 5-week monkey study design.
dose.note: Monkeys given SC epcoritamab had lower, delayed peak levels and lower cytokines than IV, with comparable B-cell depletion and bioavailability.
dose.quote: Peak plasma levels of DuoBody-CD3xCD20 were lower and delayed after subcutaneous administration, which was associated with a reduction in plasma cytokine levels compared to intravenous administration, while bioavailability was comparable.
dose.judgement: Opening entry. The monkey study stated a regimen target (SC dosing gives B-cell depletion at lower peak cytokines), not a human mg dose.

dose.magnitude_basis: SC regimen: B-cell depletion reached with modest cytokine rise
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed). Mixed B-NHL escalation (FL subset); NCT03625037 first posted 2018-08-10, no results posted.
dose.note: SC epcoritamab to 60 mg reached robust B-cell depletion with modest cytokine increases and no grade 3+ CRS; MTD not reached.
dose.short: SC regimen reached depletion, mild CRS
dose.quote: Epcoritamab induced robust and sustained B-cell depletion, and CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell activation and expansion, with modest increases in cytokine levels.
dose.reason: SC regimen held as monkeys predicted
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the route/regimen prediction (SC keeps depletion while lowering cytokine peaks) is scored as a dose-regimen target that was reached and tolerated; no NOAEL/HNSTD-based margin is public, so margin_stated is false. Patients were mixed B-NHL, which the dose question allows.

dose.note: PBPK/PD model fit to escalation data predicted trimer formation plateauing at 48-96 mg and 48 mg as optimal for DLBCL and FL.
dose.quote: Model-predicted trimer formation plateaued at doses of 48 to 96 mg. Simulation results suggest that the 48-mg dose may achieve optimal response rates in DLBCL and FL.
dose.judgement: Opening entry. The model used dose-escalation patient data, but its FL dose prediction preceded the pivotal FL cohort readout, so it is prospective for that cohort.

dose.magnitude_basis: full dose at which FL response plateaus: predicted 48 mg vs observed plateau at 48-mg exposures
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); the paper updates 'a prior population pharmacokinetic model', not confirmed to be the Li 2022 PBPK/PD model, so I paired them.
dose.note: FL exposure-response analysis found response rising with exposure and a plateau at 48-mg exposures, with no CRS-exposure trend.
dose.quote: Higher epcoritamab exposure was associated with higher efficacy (ORR, CR rate, progression-free survival, overall survival; p < 0.05) with potential response rate plateau at 48-mg exposures.
dose.judgement: Paired by me (Li 2022 model, Sinnollareddy 2026 FL exposure-response). The FL cohort was dosed to the 48-mg target in 2024 (Linton 2024); the 2026 analysis is the first to show the plateau the model stated. The flat CRS-exposure relation also matched, but no tolerability margin was stated as such.

efficacy.note: Veltuzumab (IMMU-106) extended survival up to 4.2-fold in Raji-bearing SCID mice; authors expected it at least as effective as rituximab.
efficacy.quote: Treatment of Raji-bearing SCID mice with IMMU-106 yielded median survival increases of up to 4.2-fold compared with control mice.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; Raji is a Burkitt line, not FL.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: objective response in relapsed FL against predicted rituximab-like activity
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); the phase I/II's formal primary endpoint (likely safety/dose) not confirmed; registry record not located.
efficacy.note: Veltuzumab gave objective responses in 24 of 55 relapsed FL patients (44%), 27% CR/CRu, at all dose levels.
efficacy.quote: In follicular lymphoma, 24 (44%) of 55 patients had objective responses (OR), with 15 (27%) complete responses (CRs) or CRs unconfirmed (CRus) by International Working Group criteria
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. Response is the only efficacy readout of this dose-finding phase I/II; I treat it as governing. 44% ORR in rituximab-pretreated FL is in line with the 'at least as effective as rituximab' prediction, direction only.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); model list (Raji, Daudi, JeKo-1, DLBCL PDX LY2214) from FDA BLA 761324 review Table 5.
efficacy.model: Humanized-mouse lymphoma xenografts (PBMC or CD34+ engrafted)
efficacy.note: Epcoritamab reduced growth of Burkitt, mantle-cell and DLBCL PDX tumours in humanized mice; no FL model was used.
efficacy.short: Lymphoma xenografts shrank; no FL line
efficacy.quote: DuoBody-CD3xCD20 showed promising anti-tumour activity in vivo, also in the presence of excess levels of a CD20 Ab that competes for binding.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Hutchings 2021 FL responses (90% ORR, n=10) came from a trial whose primary endpoint was MTD/RP2D, so they are listed as patient_trials, not scored.

efficacy.model: Patient lymph-node B-NHL cells ex vivo (T-cell killing)
efficacy.note: Epcoritamab lysed a median 74% of primary FL tumour cells (n=15) ex vivo, irrespective of prior CD20 antibody therapy.
efficacy.short: 74% lysis of FL cells ex vivo
efficacy.quote: Median lysis of 65, 74, and 84% were achieved in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (n = 16), follicular lymphoma (n = 15), and mantle cell lymphoma (n = 8), respectively.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Published February 2021, after early FL escalation responses were presented at meetings but before the pivotal FL cohort enrolled most patients.

efficacy.note: PBPK/PD simulations predicted the 48-mg full dose may achieve optimal response rates in FL.
efficacy.short: Simulated optimal FL response at 48 mg
efficacy.quote: Simulation results suggest that the 48-mg dose may achieve optimal response rates in DLBCL and FL.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the in-silico track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour regression in mice vs IRC-assessed ORR in FL
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed). NCT03625037 has no posted results; the FL accelerated approval followed in June 2024.
efficacy.model: Humanized-mouse lymphoma xenografts (PBMC or CD34+ engrafted)
efficacy.note: EPCORE NHL-1 FL pivotal cohort: independently reviewed ORR 82.0% (105/128), CR 62.5%, at 48 mg SC.
efficacy.quote: The overall response rate was 82·0% (105 of 128 patients; 95% CI 74·3-88·3), with a complete response rate of 62·5% (80 of 128; 95% CI 53·5-70·9).

patient_trials.quote: Patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma had an overall response rate of 90% (55-100), with 50% achieving a complete response at full doses of 0·76-48 mg.
EPCORE FL-1 phase 3: epcoritamab plus R2 versus R2 in relapsed or refractory FL; FDA reports PFS HR 0.21 (Ershler 2026, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-1867).

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. The mouse models were Burkitt, MCL and DLBCL, not FL, so this is a class-level directional match. EPCORE FL-1 (phase 3, 2025) confirmed benefit in combination and changes no status.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex vivo FL lysis incl. CD20-mAb-pretreated vs ORR in anti-CD20-pretreated FL
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed). The anti-CD20-refractory subgroup ORR was not read.
efficacy.model: Patient lymph-node B-NHL cells ex vivo (T-cell killing)
efficacy.note: Pivotal FL cohort, all anti-CD20 pretreated, responded (ORR 82%), as patient FL cells predicted regardless of prior CD20 antibody.
efficacy.quote: The overall response rate was 82·0% (105 of 128 patients; 95% CI 74·3-88·3), with a complete response rate of 62·5% (80 of 128; 95% CI 53·5-70·9).
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. Eligibility required a prior anti-CD20 antibody, matching the ex-vivo claim of activity irrespective of prior CD20 mAb. Class-level, not used to pick patients.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: predicted optimal response at 48 mg vs observed ORR at 48 mg
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); the model abstract states no numeric FL ORR to compare.
efficacy.note: At the model-chosen 48 mg, the FL pivotal cohort met its ORR endpoint (82.0%).
efficacy.quote: The overall response rate was 82·0% (105 of 128 patients; 95% CI 74·3-88·3), with a complete response rate of 62·5% (80 of 128; 95% CI 53·5-70·9).
efficacy.reason: High FL response at chosen dose
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. The model claimed only that 48 mg 'may achieve optimal' FL response; a high ORR at 48 mg agrees in direction. Low confidence because 'optimal' is unquantified.

efficacy.model: Subcutaneous Daudi lymphoma xenograft in nude mice (MIL62 vs obinutuzumab/rituximab), with in-vitro ADCC
efficacy.note: MIL62 regressed Daudi xenografts in nude mice, equal to obinutuzumab and stronger than rituximab; data public only as a summary in the trial paper.
efficacy.quote: it can significantly inhibit the growth of CD20-positive human B-cell lymphoma transplanted subcutaneously in Daudi nude mice, causing tumor regression, and its activity is equivalent to obinutuzumab
efficacy.confidence_note: Model data are only summarised (no figures, no citation) in the intro of the clinical paper; year 2019 is a proxy (FIH trials registered 2019).
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; Daudi is a Burkitt line, not FL. Model year proxied by the first MIL62 trial registrations.

efficacy.model: Subcutaneous Daudi lymphoma xenograft in nude mice (MIL62 vs obinutuzumab/rituximab), with in-vitro ADCC
efficacy.note: MIL62 + lenalidomide in rituximab-failed R/R FL/MZL (94% FL): ORR 86% (43/50), meeting the pre-specified primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: Fifty patients were included in the efficacy analysis set, and 43 patients (86%, 95% CI: 73, 94) achieved objective response, meeting the pre-specified primary endpoint.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11245993). Single-arm combination with lenalidomide, so MIL62's own share is not isolated; registry NCT04110301 lists CR rate as primary while the paper's Simon two-stage design counts CR+PR; no posted registry results; phase 3 NCT04834024 unreported.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the trial paper describes the mouse data as background, which is a pairing, not a stated comparison. Scored on the paper's pre-specified ORR (Simon design on responders) rather than the registry's CR wording; FL is 94% of the population, above the 80% bar.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft tumour regression vs objective response rate
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory FL (94%) or MZL after rituximab

safety.confidence_note: FDA multidisciplinary review text in the source bundle; monkey data first public in Engelberts 2020.
safety.note: Monkeys showed first-dose cytokine release with clinical signs (one death at 1 mg/kg IV), lower after SC dosing.
safety.quote: These findings were considered associated with elevated cytokine levels, primarily following the first dose.
safety.judgement: Opening entry dated to Engelberts 2020, the first public account of the monkey cytokine data; quote taken from the FDA review, which is fuller.

safety.magnitude_basis: cytokine release in monkeys vs CRS incidence/grade in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); mixed B-NHL escalation with an FL subset; FL-only CRS figures from Linton 2024 abstract.
safety.note: CRS occurred in 59% (all grade 1-2) of escalation patients on SC step-up dosing; FL pivotal later 65% grade 1-2, 2% grade 3.
safety.quote: common adverse events were pyrexia (47 patients [69%]), primarily associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS; 40 [59%], all grade 1-2), and injection site reactions (32 [47%]; 31 grade 1).
safety.judgement: Paired by me. The named harm (cytokine release) appeared, attenuated by SC step-up as the monkey SC/IV comparison suggested. Not scored as misses: ICANS (6% in FL) and neutropenia (25% grade 3-4 in FL), because neutralizing ADAs cut monkey exposure after the first doses, so the 5-week study could not show late or neurological effects reliably.

safety.model: Soluble-format human whole-blood cytokine release assay (epcoritamab)
safety.note: Epcoritamab released IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFNg and TNFa in human whole blood from 1.6 ng/mL, none at or below 0.32 ng/mL.
safety.quote: Epcoritamab at ≥1600 pg/mL was associated with concentration-related cytokine release (IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFNγ, and TNFα).
safety.confidence_note: Non-GLP study described in the FDA review; study date not given, 2017 is a proxy from the pre-IND meeting on the nonclinical package (14 Aug 2017).
safety.judgement: Opening entry; a separate human ex-vivo system from the monkey track, so its own model_id.

safety.model: Soluble-format human whole-blood cytokine release assay (epcoritamab)
safety.note: The predicted cytokine release appeared as CRS in 59% (all grade 1-2) of B-NHL escalation patients; assay data public only with the 2023 review.
safety.quote: common adverse events were pyrexia (47 patients [69%]), primarily associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS; 40 [59%], all grade 1-2), and injection site reactions (32 [47%]; 31 grade 1).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level patient side; mixed B-NHL escalation with an FL subset (FL pivotal later 65% grade 1-2, 2% grade 3). Dated 2023, when the assay result first became public in the FDA review.
safety.judgement: Paired by me (FDA review reports the assay and clinical CRS in separate sections without comparing them). The assay names a harm in kind, not a grade or an exposure threshold in patients, so magnitude is direction only.
safety.magnitude_basis: in-vitro cytokine release vs CRS incidence in patients
